content.title: How UConn held off Illinois in the Final Four to advance to men's NCAA Tournament championship game
content.text: The Huskies reached Monday's championship game with a 71-62 win over the Illini in the national semifinalsSolo Ball, left, and Jaylin Stewart celebrate UConn's win tonight over Illinois. Getty ImagesSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMonday night's odds Getty Images Both Michigan and UConn got off to hot starts in Saturday’s Final Four games. The Huskies had to endure a push from Illinois while the Wolverines ran away from Arizona. Considering Michigan’s dominant play, it’s no surprise the Wolverines are big favorites for Monday’s national championship game.Michigan is favored by 7.5 points on DraftKings, BetMGM and FanDuel. The Wolverines opened as a 6.5-point favorite on FanDuel, but that number quickly moved so that all three sportsbooks showed matching odds.First look at Monday night Getty Images The stage is set. UConn and Michigan will play for the national championship in men’s basketball on Monday night in Indianapolis.The No. 2-seeded Huskies, seeking a third title in four seasons, dispatched No. seed 3 Illinois 71-62. Top-seeded Michigan routed fellow No. 1 Arizona 91-73, adding a fourth blowout win to its five-game run through this NCAA Tournament.The results on Saturday ensured a historic result in the title game. No program has won three championships in four years since John Wooden’s UCLA teams more than years ago. And it’s been longer than a quarter-century since a Big Ten team — Michigan State in 2000 — hoisted the trophy.Hurley on AuriemmaSpeaking with a group of reporters Saturday after his UConn men’s basketball team beat Illinois to advance to the national championship game, coach Dan Hurley offered words of support for Geno Auriemma, who coaches the UConn women’s team.Auriemma shocked many observers with his outburst near the end of his team’s 62-48 loss to South Carolina in Friday night’s semifinal game. As time expired, Auriemma got into an argument with South Carolina coach Dawn Staley in the handshake line before storming off the court without his team.Hurley is known for his hot-headedness and recently went viral for staring down and butting heads with a referee after UConn guard Braylon Mullins’ game-winning 3-pointer in an Elite Eight win over Duke.“Obviously, I’ve had a negative influence on Geno,” Hurley said, eliciting laughter. “And it’s crazy, because Geno’s helped me so much,” Hurley continued. “The way he handled the whole thing, such a stand-up guy, with the way he handled it with the statement, and he’s one of the classiest people.”Underwood gets emotional Getty ImagesBrad Underwood is full of emotion talking postgame.💬 “This team, like I said, gave me joy because they were about all the right things. If you want to put a contest together about good human beings, we’ll win. There’s no question what this group will be in life. As a coach, that’s why I got in this. Am I competitive? Does today stink? It hurts. My gut hurts so bad right now that I feel for all of them.”“We’ve got great people. We’ve got great support. For that, I’ll reflect at some time. Today is not a very good time to ask me that. But I’ll reflect on what we’re doing. I feel sad. I’m sad. If you want to know the truth, I’m sad. … I’m going to steal a quote from Kelvin Sampson. I may not be as big a part of their life, but they are my life, and I’m sad.”Wagler on the Illini Getty ImagesKeaton Wagler on the Illini locker room postgame:💬 “There was a lot of emotions, a lot of tears. I think that’s just how hard we worked this whole year. You never want the season to end. That’s what it was. I think we had a really great season, a special season, making history. I love each and every one of my teammates, and I wouldn’t have wanted to do it with anyone else.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMore from Underwood Getty ImagesMore from Illinois head coach Brad Underwood:💬 “I’m really bad at the end of seasons, guys. I’m terrible. I’ve been doing this a long time, and I’ve never been around a group of guys who have given me more joy. We didn’t have bad practices. They played for the name on the front. Andrej (Stojakovic) came here with the intent of being around winning and being a part of that, and this young man has grown to a whole new level. I couldn’t be prouder of him.“I think they (Illinois fans) fell in love with this group because of who they are as people. It’s just an extremely high-character locker room. Endings stink. … today was not our day. I want them to all hold their head high and feel proud of the jersey they wore. I’m selfish here when I say this, the joy that they gave me this year was very, very meaningful.”Underwood on the loss Getty ImagesHere’s what Brad Underwood had to say to start Illinois’ news conference:“A lot of credit to UConn. They fight. They compete. Very, very good basketball team. Seemed like we were fighting uphill all day. I felt really good at half being down eight. They were 42 percent on twos. They banked one in.”“I liked our looks. Even though we were 3 of 14 from 3, I liked every one of our looks. I thought defensively it was the tempo that we wanted. I thought we were really solid.”“We fought, we fought, we fought, and had a very tough shooting night, especially at the rim. We missed some shots that we normally don’t miss. It’s part of this game. The ball has to go in. … I thought our looks were really good, and I wouldn’t do anything on that side over again.”More of your views on tonight's gameAnd here are what some of our readers on our Discuss tab had to say about UConn’s win: Getty ImagesDan Hurley on his program: 💬 “We’re a tough program. We’re a tough program. We’re a group of fighters. It’s not appealing to everyone. I’m sure there’s some people in here that it’s off-putting for. But we are a group of fighters. We are incredibly tough. We’ve got incredible will. We go into these games, we’re ready for battle.”Hurley on Demary Getty Images Dan Hurley was asked about Silas Demary Jr.'s critical offensive rebound that led to Braylon Mullins’ late 3. Hurley used it as a chance to reiterate his dissatisfaction with being tonight’s underdog:💬 “Yeah, we knew what it was. You’re coming into the game as an underdog versus a team that you beat by 13 points earlier in the season, which was kind of surprising, that that’s how we kind of came into the game.“Obviously I’ve been waiting to say that and now I forgot your question.”He then went on to actually answer the question.💬 “What he’s (Demary) done for our basketball team, the mentality, it was everything we were lacking last year, just a guard like him, ball hawk, incredible toughness, on the backboard. Made (Keaton) Wagler work for it, made (Kylan) Boswell, just his on ball defense. He’s a shell of himself offensively. He is really gutting it out, and the courage he has showed, I think, has been inspiring for the group.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementA reader's thoughts on UConn ... and Hurley Getty Images We’ve received an email from Robert Y. about UConn’s win over Illinois. Here’s what Robert had to say:UCONN had the better team and the better coach! Illinois took far too many shots beyond the 3-point line. Shot selection was poor throughout the game, and UCONN played excellent defense.Remember, you can share your thoughts on tonight’s Final Four action by sending us an email at live@theathletic.com.Reed remains reliable Getty Images The fact that Tarris Reed Jr. had only 17 points tonight says more about UConn inexplicably going away from him in the second half than it does his overall body of work. Reed turned in a 17-point, 11-rebound double-double on 6-of-12 shooting, and he went a perfect 5-of-5 from the line. His reward? A heavyweight matchup with the uber-talented frontcourt of either Arizona or Michigan.Mullins on opening 3-pointer Getty Images Braylon Mullins on his game-opening 3-pointer: 💬 “I think it was the flow of the game, but coming into the game, I knew I needed to shoot it with confidence coming off last Sunday, just to have that flow, boosts all the confidence for you to keep shooting within the game.”Wagler goes out strong Getty Images It will come as little solace for Keaton Wagler tonight when he learns he was the game’s leading scorer, with 20 points on 7-for-16 shooting in Illinois’ losing effort. Wagler struggled mightily from deep, going just 2-for-10 from 3-point range, but he showed the athleticism and finesse around the rim that make him such an exciting NBA Draft prospect. His performance tonight, despite the loss, gave plenty of flashes of the talent that will likely see him get his name called early in Brooklyn in June.More from Hurley Getty Images More from UConn head coach Dan Hurley on his team's win tonight over Illinois: 💬 “Couldn’t be more proud of my guys and how hard they fought when most people probably didn’t think we were going to win the game, or at least a little bit of what I saw on TV today, you know, TNT and some of the different prognostications.“So it was great to win the game. I had to throw some shade.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementWelcome home, Braylon Mullins Getty Images Once again, Braylon Mullins was at the center of the action for UConn in the Huskies' return to the Final Four — a short drive from his hometown in Indiana.Fresh off his already-iconic 3-pointer to beat Duke in the Elite Eight, Mullins got the scoring started in the game’s opening minutes and hit the de facto dagger in the game’s closing minutes — both, of course, via 3-pointers.Mullins finished with 15 points on just just 5-for-14 shooting from the field, but he was 4-for-7 from 3 and made those four makes count.UConn makes it hurt from deep Getty Images UConn only shot 35 percent from the field, just a hair better than Illinois' 34 percent shooting.But the Huskies took a larger-than-usual amound of 3s, 33, and made 12 of them for a 36 percent rate from deep. That was a major difference in this game, especially when factoring Illinois’ uncharacteristic poor shooting from beyond the arc.Pearl compares Hurley to coaching legend Getty Images Bruce Pearl: 💬 “Dan Hurley is doing stuff that John Wooden did.”Illinois struggled both times against UConn Illinois' two lowest point totals of the season came against UConn. Illini lost 74-61 to the Huskies back in November, and 71-62 in the Final Four. The Illini were held under 70 points only one other time this season: their 65-55 win over Houston in the Sweet 16.
